I have farmed in Quzhou County for over 30 years. I never went to school, but I know this land and the seasons better than any book. In our village, everyone follows the wheat–maize double-cropping system: we sow winter wheat in October and plant summer maize immediately after the wheat harvest in early June. That is the only way to make full use of the good flat land here. I have 6 mu of farmland.

My wheat is already in the ground from last autumn. I sowed *Luyuan 502*, an improved seed that gives me steady yields. Before sowing, I rotary-tilled the soil to break it up and mix in the wheat straw. Now, in early spring, I will topdress with urea and irrigate three times—at green-up, jointing, and flowering. I will spray pesticides four times to control weeds, aphids, and rust. I expect about 1,000 jin per mu.

After harvesting the wheat in early June, I will plant *Denghai 605* hybrid maize with no tillage—there is no time between crops, and the maize grows well that way. I will put down compound fertilizer at planting and irrigate twice, at jointing and grain filling. I will spray pesticides three times for weeds and corn borers. I expect about 1,100 jin per mu.

This is what I do every year, and it works.
